summary: I wrote design.md. It specifies one shared canvas and avatar, where the hero subtree and the game subtree are mutually exclusive and each owns the mixer, camera and head motion in its own mode. Physics uses @react-three/rapier 1.5.0 only for setup and teardown; the game steps the raw Rapier world itself at a fixed 60 Hz, with a cap on catch-up and its own interpolation, and the movement logic is plain TypeScript tested against real Rapier in Node. Locomotion clips are stripped offline into small rotation-only files, and a lint rule makes the single dynamic import of components/game/entry.ts the only way into game code. Per-dev constraints are in design.md section 9 (do-not-touch list and rules), section 8 (milestone-to-files table with tests and gates) and section 10 (assumptions A1-A7 and risks R1-R4, each tied to the milestone that checks it).

assumptions: A1: R3F 8 error boundaries inside the Canvas catch game errors without taking down the page. Verify in M2.
A2: in @react-three/rapier 1.5.0, useRapier().world is the raw RAPIER.World and the paused prop stops all internal stepping. Verify in M1 against the installed .d.ts.
A3: the KinematicCharacterController method names in design.md 4.4 match rapier3d-compat 0.14.0. Verify in M1.
A4: world.free() releases character controllers. This is mitigated by removing the controller explicitly in an ordered dispose that runs before unmount.
A5: the rapier3d-compat build initializes in Node under Vitest. The first M1 physics test proves or disproves it.
A6: webpack retries a failed import() chunk on the next call, so Retry works. Verify in M2.
A7: the owner downloads the Mixamo idle, jump, fall and land clips ('Without Skin') and converts them to GLB. Until then the fallbacks in design.md 5.1 apply.
Vitest and testing-library versions come from the audit's npm view checks and were not install-tested.
decisionsProposed: ADR-001: @react-three/rapier 1.5.0 and rapier3d-compat 0.14.0 pinned exactly. Physics paused is used only for init and disposal; the game owns stepping at 60 Hz with max 4 steps and a dropped backlog. Colliders are built imperatively from layout data shared with the tests.
ADR-002: one canvas. The hero subtree and the active game subtree are mutually exclusive, so exactly one owner holds the avatar scene, mixer, head motion and camera. Avatar.tsx is not edited.

ADR-003: game clips are stripped offline into public/game/clips/ (rotation only, no Hips, no root motion). Animation state comes from measured speed and grounded state; playback rate is matched to speed within a clamp.
ADR-004: Vitest with jsdom opted in per file, and physics tests run against real Rapier in Node.
ADR-005: one localStorage record 'portfolio.game.progress' with an integer version, ordered migrations, reset to default on invalid data, and an in-memory fallback.

ADR-006: .eslintrc.json extending next/core-web-vitals and deletion of eslint.config.mjs. no-restricted-imports enforces the game import boundary and bans testimonials in game code. Note: next build will now lint and fail on errors, so M1 must handle the pre-existing lint baseline.
Owner action needed before the M1 visual gate for jump, fall, land and idle: download the Mixamo clips and record them in ASSETS.md (A7).
lessonsProposed: Adding the first .eslintrc to a Next 14 repo makes next build lint too and fail on errors. Plan the pre-existing lint baseline into the same milestone as the lint fix, not later.

When a hook's async connect assigns a resource after an await with no cancellation check (useRealtimeChat.ts:144-145), a teardown during 'connecting' can be undone. Disable the triggering UI during that state rather than relying on idempotent cleanup.
Compare the spec's movement speeds with the measured clip ground speeds at design time. Here the defaults are about 2x the clip speeds, which guarantees foot sliding unless tuned or re-sourced.
